tax_litigation.status: The appeal filed by the Company against the assessment order passed under Section 143(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 has been allowed in favour of the Company, with the CIT(A) deleting the additions and disallowances made by the Assessing Officer and providing consequential relief to the Company. Further, the penalty proceedings initiated under Section 271(1)(c) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 in respect of the aforesaid additions have been directed to be dropped.

tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner of State Tax (Appeals) II, Mumbai City Division, Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: For the assessment year 2013-14, our Company (“Appellant”) has filed two appeals namely Appeal Petition No. JC/APPII/VAT-125/2018-19 and Appeal Petition No. JC/APP-II/CST-126/2018-19 before the Joint Commissioner of State Tax (Appeals) II, Mumbai City Division, Mumbai. These appeals are against the assessment order dated March 26, 2018 (“Impugned Order”) passed by the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, E-716, Nodal Division-12, Mumbai (“Assessing Authority”) under Section 23(2) of the Maharashtra Value Added Tax, 2002 (“MVAT Act”) and under Section 9(2) of the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956 (“CST Act”) read with Section 23(2) of the MVAT Act. In the appeal under the MVAT Act, the assessment order resulted in no refund and in relation to the appeal under Section 9(2) of the CST Act read with Section 23(2) of the MVAT Act, the assessment order resulted in dues amounting to ₹2.98 million. Both appeals were initially dismissed due to non-attendance and non-prosecution, which led to the confirmation of the Impugned Order. Subsequently, the Appellant filed an application for restoration of the appeal. The appeal was restored by an order dated June 11, 2024. The matter is currently pending.
